journey.title: Focus stays in the results dialog after Show all removes itself
journey.goal: Activating a control that removes itself keeps keyboard focus inside the trapped dialog

functionalJourney.title: Show all results with the pointer
functionalJourney.goal: The dialog opens, lists every result and closes

guards.title: Escape closes results and returns focus
guards.goal: Escape dismisses the dialog and focus returns to the trigger

plan.root_cause: When the currently focused node inside the focus trap is removed from the DOM, the focus trap attempts to refocus that detached node, which fails, leaving focus outside the trap (on the body). This occurs because the trap's checkFocusIn handler does not verify that the mostRecentlyFocusedNode is still attached to the DOM and within the trap's containers before attempting to refocus it.
plan.repair_strategy: Modify the checkFocusIn handler to verify that the mostRecentlyFocusedNode is still contained within one of the trap's containers before attempting to refocus it. If it is not, fall back to focusing the initial focus node (as determined by the trap's initialization logic).
plan.expected_accessibility_effect: After activating the trap and removing the focused node (via the 'Show all' button), keyboard focus will remain trapped within the dialog, specifically moving to the close button (or initial focus node) when the focused node is removed. This ensures that subsequent tab navigation remains within the dialog.
functional_risks: The trap might consume slightly more CPU when checking containment of the mostRecentlyFocusedNode on every focusin event that occurs outside the trap.

If the mostRecentlyFocusedNode is removed but another node in the trap becomes focused by the browser (unlikely), we might override that focus with the initial focus node. However, the scenario of a node being removed and the browser focusing another node in the trap is rare because the removal of the focused node typically causes the browser to focus the body or the next element in the DOM (which is likely outside the trap).

The container.contains check may not work correctly for nodes in shadow DOM if the trap is configured to use shadow DOM. However, the trap in the given usage does not enable shadow DOM support (no getShadowRoot option), so containers are plain DOM nodes and container.contains is sufficient.
verification_requirements: Verify that after clicking the 'Show all 4 results' button (which removes itself), focus is retained within the results dialog (specifically, the close button should receive focus).
Verify that tab navigation continues to work within the dialog after the button removal.
Verify that the Escape key still closes the dialog and returns focus to the open button.
Verify that the initial state of the trap (before any node removal) still functions correctly.

plan.root_cause: When the focused 'Show all 4 results' button is removed from the DOM, the browser moves focus to the body. The focus trap's checkFocusIn handler attempts to restore focus using the stale mostRecentlyFocusedNode (the removed button) or the initial focus node. However, the initial focus node is derived from state.tabbableGroups which is not updated after the button removal, and the focus() call during the focusin event may not take effect synchronously in all environments.
plan.repair_strategy: Update the tabbable nodes in checkFocusIn before attempting to restore focus, and ensure the initial focus node is computed from the current DOM. Also, defer the focus restoration via setTimeout to allow the current focus event to complete, preventing the browser from ignoring the focus() call.
plan.expected_accessibility_effect: After activating the trap and removing the focused node (via the 'Show all' button), keyboard focus will remain trapped within the dialog, moving to the close button (or initial focus node) when the focused node is removed. This ensures that subsequent tab navigation remains within the dialog.
functional_risks: The setTimeout deferral may cause a brief moment where focus is on the body before being restored, which could be perceived as a flash by screen readers.
Calling updateTabbableNodes on every focus escape adds a small performance cost, but focus escapes are rare.
If the trap is deactivated before the setTimeout fires, the focus restoration may still run but the trap is no longer active; tryFocus will early-return because state.active is false.
verification_requirements: Verify that after clicking the 'Show all 4 results' button (which removes itself), focus is retained within the results dialog (specifically, the close button should receive focus).
Verify that tab navigation continues to work within the dialog after the button removal.
Verify that the Escape key still closes the dialog and returns focus to the open button.
Verify that the initial state of the trap (before any node removal) still functions correctly.

The focus trap's checkFocusIn handler attempts to restore focus using the stale mostRecentlyFocusedNode (the removed button) or the initial focus node. However, the initial focus node is derived from state.tabbableGroups which is not updated after the button removal, and the focus() call during the focusin event may not take effect synchronously if deferred via setTimeout, causing the test to observe focus on the body before restoration occurs.
plan.repair_strategy: Update the tabbable nodes in checkFocusIn before attempting to restore focus, and perform the focus restoration synchronously (without setTimeout) to ensure focus is moved back into the dialog before the test asserts. The restoration logic will prefer the most recently focused node if it is still contained in a trap container; otherwise it will compute the current initial focus node (first tabbable node) from the updated tabbable groups.
plan.expected_accessibility_effect: After activating the trap and removing the focused node (via the 'Show all 4 results' button), keyboard focus will remain trapped within the dialog, moving to the close button (the only remaining tabbable node) when the focused node is removed. This ensures that subsequent tab navigation remains within the dialog and the focus-within assertion passes.
functional_risks: Calling updateTabbableNodes on every focus escape adds a small performance cost, but focus escapes are rare.
If the trap is deactivated before the focus restoration runs, tryFocus will early-return because state.active is false.
Synchronous focus() during a focusin event may be ignored by some browsers, but stopping immediate propagation increases the chance of success.

Verify that tab navigation continues to work within the dialog after the button removal.
